candidates.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
candidates.content: The highest viewpoint in Lisbon, at the top of the Graça hill, spread out in front of the small Capela de Nossa Senhora do Monte (founded in 1147, remodelled in the 20th century). To the south you look down over the Castelo de São

candidates.name: Castelo de São Jorge
candidates.price: , ages 13–25 , disabled or seniors 65+ , children under 12 free; guided tour
candidates.content: Humans settled on this hill as early as the 8th century BCE, and the first fortifications date from the 1st century BCE. Before the Portuguese conquest in the 1147 Siege of Lisbon, the site was successively occupied by the Phoenic

candidates.name: Lisbon Cathedral
candidates.alt: Sé de Lisboa, Igreja de Santa Maria Maior
candidates.content: Built in 1147, the cathedral has survived various earthquakes and has undergone restoration, renovation, and modification over the years. Its elements include Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles. It has been a national monument

candidates.name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
candidates.price: , seniors 65+/students/youth card , disabled & children 12 and under free
candidates.content: One of the most important national museums, dedicated to Portuguese azulejo tiles since the late 1400s. It's in the former Madre de Deus Convent, founded in 1509 by Queen Leonor.

candidates.name: Panteão Nacional
candidates.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00, platform 10:00-18:00 (closed Mondays, shorter hours in winter)
candidates.content: This is one of the most striking buildings in Lisbon. Its tall dome and white facade makes it a real landmark in Alfama/Eastern Lisbon. Excellent views from the rooftop terrace. Construction began in 1681, then halted until the do

candidates.name: Igreja do Carmo
candidates.hours: Oct-May: Mon-Sat 10:00-18:00; Jun-Sep: Mon-Sat 10:00-19:00; closed Sun, 1 Jan, 1 May, 25 Dec
candidates.content: The hilltop church of the former convent of Carmo is a towering memorial of the 1755 earthquake, which made the roof of the church collapse, but the Gothic arches of the nave survived. The church was preserved that way and now ser

candidates.name: Fundação Arpad Szenes / Vieira da Silva
candidates.content: This museum is installed in the restored 18th-century former Royal Silk Factory. Its permanent collection covers a wide time period of the works of 20th-century painters Arpad Szenes and Maria Helena Vieira da Silva, and regularly

candidates.name: Museu Colecção Berardo
candidates.content: The permanent collection of the museum consists of the Berardo Collection, which is made up of modern and contemporary art, with major art movements like abstract expressionism, Abstraction-Création, action painting, body Art, con

candidates.name: Museu Nacional dos Coches
candidates.content: Housed in the former riding school of the palace, don't miss the world's largest collection of horse-drawn coaches and other royal vehicles. One of Lisbon's many unusual museums. In the "Museum street", Belem.

candidates.name: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
candidates.content: One of the best museums in Lisbon. Created from the personal collection of the art and artifact collector Calouste Gulbenkian. The collection include Egyptian artefacts; Islamic and oriental art; paintings by masters such as Rembr

candidates.name: Pavilhão do Conhecimento - Centro Ciência Viva
candidates.alt: Pavilion of Knowledge - Living Science Centre
candidates.price: Adults , seniors 65+ , youths 12–17 , children 3–11 , children 2 & under free, family (2 adults + children under 17)
candidates.content: Ciência Viva is an interactive science and technology museum that aims to make science accessible to all, stimulating experimentation and exploration of the physical world.

candidates.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
candidates.content: Good viewpoint in Alfama uphill from the cathedral along tram route. Lovely view over rooftops and river.

candidates.name: Igreja e Mosteiro de São Vicente de Fora
candidates.alt: Monastery of St. Vincent Outside the Walls
candidates.content: Started in 1582, this Mannerist monastery wasn't completed until 1629, following the reconstruction of a 1147 church under royal decree. The church houses the Pantheon of the House of Braganza, where many monarchs, consorts, and t

candidates.name: Museu Militar de Lisboa
candidates.content: Housed in a 16th-century foundry, this museum holds its testaments to Portuguese military history, and contains many artifacts, including a sword used by Vasco da Gama.

candidates.name: Museu da Marioneta
candidates.price: Admission , ages 13–25 , 65+ or disabled , kids under 13 free; shows , kids, seniors 65+, and students under 25
candidates.content: The museum covers the history of puppetry around the world, with an emphasis on Portugal. Various types of puppets are on display.

candidates.name: Basílica da Estrela
candidates.content: This Neoclassical and Baroque basilica, dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, was built in the late 1700s by Queen Maria I in fulfilment of a vow. The Queen is entombed in the right transept. Among the artworks is a nativity sce

candidates.name: Palácio de São Bento
candidates.content: Built in 1598, the palace has served as the home of Portugal's parliament since 1834. The adjoining São Bento Mansion serves as the prime minister's residence.

candidates.name: Aqueduto das Aguas Livres
candidates.content: This is a historic aqueduct in the city of Lisbon, Portugal. It is one of the most remarkable examples of 18th-century Portuguese engineering, including the largest stone arch in the world. The main course of the aqueduct covers 1

candidates.name: Praça do Comércio
candidates.content: This magnificent plaza, facing the river, is the beginning of Lisboa's downtown. It is also known as 'Terreiro do Paço', meaning 'Grounds of the Palace', relating to its function before the Great Earthquake of 1755. The upper floo

candidates.name: Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
candidates.alt: MAAT – Museu de Arte, Arquitetura e Tecnologia
candidates.price: Adults , kids 12+/students/seniors 65+ , kids under 12 free,15 Jul–31 Aug: 20% discount off all tickets (admission includes Tejo Power Station)
candidates.hours: Wed–Mon 11:00–19:00 (Jun–Sep: Fri Sat until 22:00), closed Tue
candidates.content: This museum of contemporary art is housed in a riverside building of contemporary design.

candidates.name: Tejo Power Station
candidates.alt: Central Tejo, f/k/a Museu da Electricidade, Electricity Museum
candidates.price: Admission included in the price of the Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
candidates.content: This disused power station is now a museum dedicated to the science, industry, and history of electricity production in Portugal.

candidates.name: Centro de Arte Moderna
candidates.hours: Daily 10:00 – 18:00, closed on Tuesdays, 10:00 – 21:00 on Saturdays
candidates.content: A museum dedicated to art since the 1950s, focusing on Portuguese artists and including other nationalities, notably British and Armenian. Part of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation.

candidates.name: Museu do Teatro Romano
candidates.content: Along the way from downtown to Saint George's Castle.

candidates.name: Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga
candidates.content: Portugal's impressive national art collection, including 14-19th century European painting, artefacts of Portuguese contact with the East and Africa and a collection of ecclesiastical treasures. Highlights include Dürer's St Jerom

candidates.name: Cemitério dos Prazeres
candidates.content: This large cemetery is packed with majestic gravestones and mausoleums, separated by wide, pedestrian, tree-lined "streets". Many graves are marked with icons telling something about the person's role in historical Lisbon. A beaut

candidates.name: Lisbon Botanical Gardens
candidates.price: Entrance €5 adults, discounts for kids, seniors and students
candidates.content: A hidden gem. It was created several hundred years ago, by a King of Portugal at the time of the Discoveries. The story goes that this King wanted one of every type of plant in the world, and although that's unlikely, there is a h

candidates.name: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Conceição Velha
candidates.alt: Old Church of Our Lady of the Conception
candidates.content: 18th-century Manueline-style church, a national monument.

candidates.name: Santa Justa Lift
candidates.content: Excellent vertical view of the Baixa streets, next to Igreja do Carmo. The line can be quite long, you may want to consider walking up and riding it down instead.

candidates.name: Teleférico do Parque das Nações
candidates.price: Adults one-way, round-trip; kids 4–12 one-way, round-trip; kids 0–3 free
candidates.content: An aerial tramway built for Expo '98. It operates between the Oceanarium and the Vasco da Gama Tower and offers excellent views of the fairgrounds, the river, the bridge, and beyond.

candidates.name: Teatro Nacional Dona Maria II
candidates.content: The most famous live theatre stage in Lisbon. The Neoclassical and Palladian building was built in the 1840s and has been a national monument since 2003.

candidates.name: Monsanto Forest Park
candidates.content: A municipal protected forest, the largest green patch in the city, covering almost 10 km². It offers a well-diversified, tree-covered area. 50 ha is set aside as the Ecological Park, which runs an interpretation centre, with space

candidates.name: Altice Arena
candidates.alt: formerly MEO Arena, originally Pavilhão Atlântico
candidates.content: This 20,000-seat arena hosts touring rock bands and Brazilian musicians.

candidates.name: Casino Lisboa
candidates.content: Among the gambling opportunities here are slot machines, poker, roulette, black jack, and baccarat. They have two restaurants, four bars, two entertainment venues, and an art gallery.

candidates.name: Peixe em Lisboa
candidates.content: A food festival, with focus on fish dishes.

candidates.name: Dias da Música em Belém
candidates.content: A music festival held in Belém in western Lisbon.

candidates.name: IndieLisboa
candidates.content: An independent film festival. In addition to screenings there is also a large number of lectures and seminars.

candidates.name: Rock in Rio Lisboa
candidates.hours: Late May or early June every other year (every even numbered year)
candidates.content: A major rock music festival, branched from the famous Rock in Rio de Janeiro.

candidates.name: Jazz em Agosto
candidates.content: A annual jazz festival organized by the Gulbenkian Foundation.

candidates.name: Coliseu dos Recreios
candidates.content: Large multi-purpose auditorium for musical performances.

candidates.name: Teatro Maria Vitória
candidates.content: Presenting teatro de revista, Portuguese-style comedy revues. The theatre opened in 1922 and was restored in 1990 following a 1986 fire.

candidates.name: Lisboa em Fado
candidates.content: A typical Portuguese Fado concert hall with daily evening shows. Run by a young Fado guitarist from Lisbon. The show lasts about one hour.

candidates.name: Gulbenkian Music
candidates.content: The Gulbenkian Foundation has its own symphony orchestra and ballet group. There are also two stages operated by the foundation. One major auditorium inside the main building, and an outdoors stage in the nearby Gulbenkian Gardens

candidates.name: English Comedy Showcase
candidates.content: Featuring Portuguese and international acts doing their sets in English. A great way to get a deep cultural insight into life in Lisbon through laughter. Usually free entry and donation based.

candidates.name: Festas dos Santos
candidates.content: A number of large fiestas celebrating different catholic Saints, with parades during the day and fire work shows by night. The first and largest fiesta celebrates Saint Anthony on 13 June. It is followed by the celebration of Sain

candidates.name: Selva Comedy Cafe: Life in Lisboa - A cultural comedy show
candidates.content: This comedy show is 100% in English and features well known comedians from the local and international scene in Lisbon. The comedians have experienced dating disasters, rental nightmares, cultural quirks, and they will tell it all

candidates.name: Moda Lisboa
candidates.content: Lisbon Fashion Week.

candidates.name: Quake - Lisbon Earthquake Centre
candidates.alt: Quake - Centro do Terramoto de Lisboa
candidates.content: A fully interactive museum on the Lisbon Earthquake of 1755.

candidates.name: Café A Brasileira
candidates.price: Prices are in three levels, depending on where you choose to drink: cheapest standing at the counter, and most expensive sitting outside on the terrace
candidates.content: One of Lisbon's remaining classic cafés, with a restaurant in the basement; despite renovation, not much has changed since the 1920s. The café was Fernando Pessoa's favourite place, and a statue of the poet/philosopher stands outs

candidates.name: Tivoli Hotel Sky Bar
candidates.content: The superbly located rooftop bar of Tivoli Hotel is a small secret. On warm evenings one of the best places to have an overpriced late drink. Youngish music late night.

candidates.name: Café Martinho da Arcada
candidates.content: Established in 1782, this is the oldest continuously-operating café in Lisbon and throughout its history has been associated with important politicians, writers, and intellectuals. Writer Fernando Pessoa had a permanent table rese

candidates.name: Chafariz do Vinho
candidates.content: Perfect place to linger over a glass of wine at this wine bar that is under the arches of the city's former acquaducts. With a great selection of appetizers that are matched perfectly with the wine, it's a pleasant way to spend an

candidates.name: Portas do Sol
candidates.content: A cafe and bar on a "Miradouro", viewing spot, and thus offer a spectacular view over the Alfama rooftops down to the river.

candidates.name: Garrafeira Alfaia
candidates.content: Nice wine bar with an impressive selection of good wines and appetizers. Good place to spend the late afternoon, before going out to dinner.

candidates.name: Tasca do Chico
candidates.content: A cramped but authentic Fado bar.

candidates.name: Bar Trobadores
candidates.content: Medieval bar in downtown with a cozy atmosphere and a diverse range of traditional Portuguese delicacies. National and international beers.

candidates.name: Pois Café
candidates.content: It's a place to relax, read a book, drink a coffee and plan your way around Lisbon. Also offers toasts, pastas, quiches and salads; features late breakfasts.

candidates.name: Manteigaria - Fábrica de Pastéis de Nata
candidates.content: A bakery serving some of the best pastéis de nata in town, arguably the best in Lisbon. You can even watch them make the pasteis de nata. Standing room only.

candidates.name: Pastéis de Belém
candidates.content: The most famous of pastelarias, and justly so. They are served right out of the oven there, with the side of confectioner's sugar and cinnamon. As you navigate through the tile-covered labyrinthine passages of the expansive shop,

candidates.name: Lux Fragil
candidates.content: It's in a former warehouse and part owned by American actor John Malkovich.

candidates.name: Fado In Chiado
candidates.content: Fado In Chiado - Daily show (except on Sundays) at 19:00, with a duration of 50 minutes. Voices that sing the Fado to the sound of Portuguese guitar.

candidates.name: Time Out Market
candidates.content: The late 19th-century market was closed in 2000, and in 2014 the publisher Time Out Portugal transformed the space into a gourmet food court with 40 kiosks, including restaurants, bars, and shops. A number of Lisbon's top chefs ha

candidates.name: Rosa da Rua Restaurante
candidates.content: A traditional restaurant offering an interesting mix of Portuguese, Indian, and Cape Verdean flavours. The lunch-time buffet offers excellent value for money and great quality food. Staff are patient with English speakers.

candidates.name: Restaurante Sacramento do Chiado
candidates.content: A popular locals' place in palace stables from the 18th-century . The atmosphere and the food are excellent. Service is very good and the recommendations by the staff are outstanding. The writing on the menu is very small and diff

candidates.name: Come Prima
candidates.content: Traditional Italian fresh pasta dishes, various starters, risottos, meats and wood-oven pizzas are produced from a wide selection of prime quality fresh ingredients. Extensive wine list procured from both national and Italian prod

candidates.name: Café Buenos Aires
candidates.content: A good and selected combination of cheap and mid range dishes. The owners are very friendly and speak English, as well as Portuguese. It is a good restaurant if you want to eat South American grilled meat.

candidates.name: Restaurante Santa Rita
candidates.content: Authentic, cheap Portuguese dishes in a very busy, shared-table restaurant.

candidates.name: Malmequer Bemmequer
candidates.content: Friendly and inexpensive; long menu of traditional Portuguese dishes.

candidates.name: Restaurante Lisboa À Noite
candidates.content: A restaurant with a variety of traditional Portuguese dishes very appreciated by the tourists. Friendly environment, great service. Make sure you try the appetizers.

candidates.name: Restaurante Sinal Vermelho
candidates.content: Good traditional Portuguese at reasonable prices.

candidates.name: Belcanto
candidates.content: Contemporary Portuguese cuisine with two Michelin stars.

candidates.name: Alma
candidates.content: Two-Michelin-star fine dining by chef Henrique Sá Pessoa, blending traditional Portuguese cuisine with Asian influences. Choose from two tasting menus or order à la carte.

candidates.name: Loco Restaurante
candidates.content: Michelin-starred restaurant offering two tasting menus using local ingredients by chef Alexandre Silva, who won the first series of Top Chef de Portugal.

candidates.name: Feira da Ladra
candidates.content: A lively outdoor market offering new and used products. Markets of this type have pleased bargain hunters since the 12th century in Lisbon and the Feira da Ladra name has been around since the 17th century.

candidates.name: Mercado de Campo de Ourique
candidates.content: An indoor market selling wide selection of fruits, vegetables, meats, fish, and jewelry. A perfect break while Tram 28 turns around, it's calmer and less crowded than other markets listed.

candidates.name: Centro Vasco da Gama
candidates.content: A large shopping mall in the Parque Expo, featuring many international brands and a food court. There are 170 stores, including 33 restaurants, a health club, a hypermarket, and a 6-screen cinema.

candidates.name: El Corte Inglés
candidates.content: The Spanish department store chain invaded Lisbon, armed with cinema and supermarket. It can be a bit pricey but with good quality items.

december.text: Lisbon enjoys a Subtropical-Mediterranean climate, with mild winters and very warm summers. Strongly influenced by the Gulf Stream it is one of the mildest climates in Europe.
